# Summary of the British National Party (BNP) 2010 Manifesto

The BNP's 2010 manifesto, titled "Democracy, Freedom, Culture and Identity," presents a far-right nationalist platform centered on several core themes.

## Immigration and Demographics
The manifesto's primary focus is opposition to immigration, claiming indigenous British people face becoming a minority within 50 years. The BNP proposed halting all immigration, deporting illegal immigrants, ending asylum, and promoting voluntary repatriation. They advocated repealing the Race Relations Act and abolishing multicultural policies, while recognizing the right of "law-abiding minorities" to remain.

## European Union
The party demanded immediate EU withdrawal, arguing the organization threatens British sovereignty. They proposed redirecting EU membership fees (approximately £15 billion annually) toward domestic infrastructure and services.

## Islam and Counter-Terrorism
The manifesto contains extensive anti-Islamic content, proposing bans on burkas, mosque construction, and ritual slaughter. It called for halting Muslim immigration entirely and deporting "radical Islamist preachers."

## Economic Policy
Economically, the BNP advocated protectionism, opposing globalization and outsourcing. They proposed raising personal tax allowances to £12,500, reintroducing married couple's allowances, cutting foreign aid (£9.1 billion), and redirecting funds domestically. They supported separating retail and investment banking.

## Defense and Foreign Policy
The party proposed withdrawing troops from Afghanistan, renegotiating NATO membership, and adopting a non-interventionist foreign policy based solely on British interests.

## Social Policies
Other proposals included restoring grammar schools, increasing state pensions to £150 weekly, renationalizing railways, investing in nuclear energy while rejecting climate change theory, and introducing capital punishment for certain crimes.

The manifesto positioned the BNP as defending traditional British identity against what it characterized as existential demographic and cultural threats.
